[AMD] Drop the workaround for swizzle reorder (#12810)

Revert https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/pull/11169. This workaround
is no longer needed after LLVM PR
https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/232016. The convert can still
safely use `ds_read_b64`, tested on MI355X.

Signed-off-by: Pengzhan Zhao <borontion@gmail.com>

[AMD] Preserve store coalescing when bypassing epilogue relayouts (#12714)

This change aims to address a performance drop since #11704.
AITER’s BF16 RMSNorm benchmark bench_fused_rmsnorm_add
at **8192 × 4095** on gfx950 got bandwidth dropped by 27%.

In that case (similar to added lit), the computation layout holds
`sizePerThread = [8]`, while the coalesced store layout holds
`sizePerThread = [1]`. Removing the relayout keeps scalar
`buffer_store_short` instructions but spaces adjacent lanes’ writes 16
bytes apart instead of 2 bytes. The resulting increase in memory
requests outweighs the saved LDS accesses and barriers.

So this change try to preserve the store coalescing for some out stride
unaligned situation(store layout with sizePerThread=[1]).

For BF16/FP16, the maxElems = 8. the other profitability checks would
be:

| Source run | Destination run | Main check | New check |
|---:|---:|---|---|
| 8 | 1 | Bypass | Keep relayout |
| 1 | 8 | Keep relayout | Keep relayout |
| 8 | 8 | Bypass | Bypass |
| 8 | 16 | Bypass | Bypass |
| 16 | 8 | Bypass | Bypass |

@@ -230,6 +230,32 @@ module attributes {"ttg.num-ctas" = 1 : i32, "ttg.num-warps" = 2 : i32, ttg.targ
 
 // -----
 
+// An unaligned row requires scalar stores. With eight elements per thread,
+// consecutive lanes would store sixteen bytes apart instead of two.
+// CHECK-LABEL: rmsnorm_unaligned_row
+// CHECK:       %[[VAL:.+]] = ttg.convert_layout %{{.*}} : tensor<4096xbf16, #blocked> -> tensor<4096xbf16, #blocked1>
+// CHECK:       tt.store %{{.*}}, %[[VAL]], %{{.*}} : tensor<4096x!tt.ptr<bf16>, #blocked1>
+#blocked = #ttg.blocked<{sizePerThread = [8], threadsPerWarp = [64], warpsPerCTA = [4], order = [0]}>
+#blocked1 = #ttg.blocked<{sizePerThread = [1], threadsPerWarp = [64], warpsPerCTA = [4], order = [0]}>
+module attributes {"ttg.num-ctas" = 1 : i32, "ttg.num-warps" = 4 : i32, ttg.target = "hip:gfx950", "ttg.threads-per-warp" = 64 : i32} {
+  tt.func public @rmsnorm_unaligned_row(%arg0: !tt.ptr<bf16> {tt.divisibility = 16 : i32}, %stride: i32, %n: i32) {
+    %value = arith.constant dense<1.0> : tensor<4096xbf16, #blocked>
+    %row = tt.get_program_id x : i32
+    %base = arith.muli %row, %stride : i32
+    %row_ptr = tt.addptr %arg0, %base : !tt.ptr<bf16>, i32
+    %ptrs = tt.splat %row_ptr : !tt.ptr<bf16> -> tensor<4096x!tt.ptr<bf16>, #blocked1>
+    %offsets = tt.make_range {start = 0 : i32, end = 4096 : i32} : tensor<4096xi32, #blocked1>
+    %ptr = tt.addptr %ptrs, %offsets : tensor<4096x!tt.ptr<bf16>, #blocked1>, tensor<4096xi32, #blocked1>
+    %bound = tt.splat %n : i32 -> tensor<4096xi32, #blocked1>
+    %mask = arith.cmpi slt, %offsets, %bound : tensor<4096xi32, #blocked1>
+    %converted = ttg.convert_layout %value : tensor<4096xbf16, #blocked> -> tensor<4096xbf16, #blocked1>
+    tt.store %ptr, %converted, %mask : tensor<4096x!tt.ptr<bf16>, #blocked1>
+    tt.return
+  }
+}
+

 // The two layouts disagree on the order, so bypass is not profitable.
 // CHECK-LABEL: fma_blocked_order_mismatch
 // CHECK:       %[[VAL:.+]] = ttg.convert_layout %{{.*}} : tensor<64x128xf32, #blocked> -> tensor<64x128xf32, #blocked1>

[NVIDIA] Share identical terminal ConSan assertion reports (#12792)

ConSan-instrumented NVIDIA kernels can contain hundreds of identical
terminal `__assertfail` blocks after LLVM optimization. Share terminal
blocks only when the complete assertion calls, ABI, debug locations, and
terminal behavior match. Preserve every original check and distinct
diagnostic. Enable the pass only for CUDA ConSan compilation.

GB300, eight representative numerical cases, two fresh-cache runs per
compiler against main (alternating order after first-use
initialization):
- Mean cold test time: 4.969 → 4.612 s (7.17% faster).
- ConSan compilation, total over 11 instrumented kernels: 26.718 →
23.930 s (10.43% faster).
- All compilation, 47 kernels: 34.039 → 31.225 s (8.27% faster).
- All 32 numerical cases passed; each run compiled the same 47 kernels,
including 11 with ConSan. Two runs per arm are an estimate, not a
statistical confidence bound.

Historical isolated GPU replay on an older base: 37.329 → 37.390 ms for
17 ConSan launches (effectively flat, +0.16%; two measured replays after
one warmup). Fresh paired measurements above cover cold tests and
compilation, not GPU events.

Validation: native `make`; `lit -v test/LLVMIR/break-phi-struct.ll`
(passed). The regression checks sharing, distinct diagnostics,
observable effects, and distinct debug locations. Full stacked ConSan
diagnostic suite on GB300: 504 passed, 75 skipped.

Active review and landing order: this PR → #12795 (concurrent file-cache
builds) → #12796 (single-CTA shadow locks). #12795 and #12796 are
independent siblings based directly on this PR.

#12793 (liveness analysis) and #12794 (masked tracking stores) are on
hold and are not part of the active landing stack.

[Pipeliner] Predicate conditionals through a pure branch (#12773)

Prevent inactive pipeline stages from executing effectful branches by
selecting a pure branch when available or guarding the entire
conditional otherwise.

[PIPELINER] Check the op's cluster against clusters.end(), not Cluster{} (#12801)

`CoarseSchedule::getOpsInOrder`([Schedule.cpp#L168](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/459a62be445a746099aad7bd4b76f18f64916e59/lib/Dialect/TritonGPU/Transforms/Pipeliner/Schedule.cpp#L168))
asserts
```cpp
assert(cluster != Cluster{} && "Op with invalid cluster!");
```

`Cluster` is a `std::list<int>::iterator`
([Schedule.h#L94](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/459a62be445a746099aad7bd4b76f18f64916e59/include/triton/Dialect/TritonGPU/Transforms/Schedule.h#L94)),
so this compares an iterator into `clusters` with a value-initialized
iterator that belongs to no list. The standard only defines comparing
value-initialized
iterators with each other, so this comparison is undefined. libstdc++
and libc++ in their default modes happen to accept it, but checked STL
iterators reject the comparison itself:

- MSVC Debug (`_ITERATOR_DEBUG_LEVEL=2`): "list iterators incompatible".
- libstdc++ `_GLIBCXX_DEBUG` (enabled by
`LLVM_ENABLE_EXPENSIVE_CHECKS`):
"attempt to compare a dereferenceable (start-of-sequence) iterator to a
  singular (value-initialized) iterator".

Because the comparison is rejected regardless of the iterator's value,
the assert fires for every scheduled op, even on a valid schedule.
`serialize()`

([Schedule.cpp#L256](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/459a62be445a746099aad7bd4b76f18f64916e59/lib/Dialect/TritonGPU/Transforms/Pipeliner/Schedule.cpp#L256))
calls `getOpsInOrder()`, so any software-pipelined loop aborts on such
builds. We hit it compiling a pipelined dot loop for gfx1150 through

[rocmlirTriton](https://github.com/ROCm/rocmlirTriton/blob/32481957048683dc12a1a75f8a502599c0bb844b/cmake/triton.cmake#L22-L25)
in an MSVC Debug build.

Compare against `clusters.end()`, which is what "no cluster" means for
an iterator into this list. Release builds are unaffected: the assert is
compiled
out under `NDEBUG`.

[Pipeliner] Wait before single-buffer MMAv5 accumulator resets (#12797)

A conditional nonzero reset can overwrite a single-buffer MMAv5
accumulator before the preceding asynchronous MMA completes.

```python
acc = tl.zeros((256, 16), tl.float32)
for k in range(6):
    acc = tl.dot(A.load([0, k * 128]), B.load([k * 128, 0]), acc)
    if k % 2 == 0:
        C.store([0, 0], acc)
    if k % 4 == 3:
        acc = tl.full((256, 16), 1.0, tl.float32)
```
